panel: notebook: Under the hood (What for...of asks for)
what: The notebook says for...of over a string "goes by whole characters, so an emoji is one lap". for...of actually steps by code points: a smiley is one lap, but a joined emoji such as a family is several. Chapter 22 makes exactly this distinction, so ch6 overstates it.
evidence: Scratch run on Node 22.23.4: `for (const ch of "\u{1F468}\u200D\u{1F469}\u200D\u{1F467}")` runs 5 laps. The ch22 plan: a family emoji is "5 code points but 1 grapheme via Intl.Segmenter".
fix: Change it to: "For strings, for...of goes by code points, so a simple emoji like a smiley is one lap (unlike s[i], which reads UTF-16 code units). Emoji glued together from several parts still take several laps: Chapter 22."
